title: Primary Function of the Tapered Shaft
learningObjectives: Identify the shaft's role in the drive or test system.
student: State the primary mechanical function of the tapered shaft.
instructor: The shaft transmits torque between the input coupling and the fixed or driven machine interface while limiting rotational compliance.

title: External Torsional Loading
learningObjectives: Identify the load entering the shaft.
student: Identify the externally applied mechanical load and where it enters the system.
instructor: A shaft-axis torque T is applied at end A through the input coupling.

title: Fixed-End Boundary Condition
learningObjectives: State the rotational restraint at the large end.
student: Identify the torsional boundary condition at the large end and explain its mechanical consequence.
instructor: The large end is fixed against rotation, so its angular displacement is zero and the interface develops a reaction torque.

title: Torque Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace torque transfer from input to support.
student: Trace the torque load path from the input coupling to the support.
instructor: The path is input coupling, small-radius end A, continuously varying shaft, fixed interface, and machine frame.

title: Expected Compliance-Dominating Region
learningObjectives: Predict where most shaft twist will accumulate.
student: Before calculating, identify the shaft region expected to contribute most strongly to total twist and explain why.
instructor: The small-radius region near A should dominate because J is proportional to r4 and local torsional compliance is proportional to 1/r4.

title: Parameters Governing Twist
learningObjectives: Identify inputs controlling the angle of twist.
student: Identify the geometric, loading, and material parameters governing the angle of twist.
instructor: The governing parameters are applied torque T, shaft length L, radius function r(x), and shear modulus G.

title: Why Integration Is Required
learningObjectives: Explain why a constant-section twist formula is insufficient.
student: Explain why the constant-section equation φ = TL/(JG) cannot be used directly.
instructor: The radius and polar moment vary with position, so local differential twist must be integrated along the shaft. No single constant J represents the actual geometry.

title: Student-Generated Tapered-Shaft Idealization
learningObjectives: Create a variable-radius torsion model before viewing the reference figure.
student: Before using the reference figure, draw a solid circular shaft of length L with coordinate x measured from end A, applied torque T at A, and zero rotation at the opposite end. Label r(x), J(x), and the internal torque.
instructor: A valid model shows a solid nonprismatic circular shaft carrying constant internal torque, with x measured from A and zero rotation at the fixed large end.
gradingNotes: Students should attempt the idealization before seeing the instructor reference figure.

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State assumptions supporting the nonprismatic torsion model.
student: State the assumptions needed for the base torsion model.
instructor: Assume Saint-Venant torsion of a solid circular shaft, homogeneous isotropic linear-elastic material, constant G, small rotation, and torque applied about the shaft axis. Neglect bending, axial loading, local stress concentrations, attachment flexibility, and warping effects.

title: Mechanics Analysis Plan
student: Write the calculation sequence before substituting values.
instructor: Determine the reaction and internal torque; define the nondimensional coordinate and radius law; write J(x) = πr(x)4/2; use dφ = T dx/[GJ(x)]; integrate from 0 to L; calculate stress; and interpret the result.

title: Boundary Condition and Reaction Torque
student: State the fixed-end rotational boundary condition and determine the reaction torque.
instructor: The fixed-end rotation is zero. Static equilibrium gives a reaction torque of magnitude {{taper_reaction_Nm}} N·m, opposite the applied torque.

title: Internal Torque Distribution
learningObjectives: Determine internal torque throughout the shaft.
instructor: Because no additional torques act along the shaft, Tint(x) = T throughout 0 ≤ x ≤ L.

title: Radius Function and Variable Polar Moment
learningObjectives: Write a dimensionally consistent radius law and variable polar moment.
student: Define a dimensionally consistent radius function and write the polar moment of inertia as a function of position.
instructor:
Define ξ = x/(1 m). Then r(x) = r0[1 + ξ3/2 + ξ5/2] and J(x) = πr(x)4/2.

For the assigned geometry, r(0) = {{taper_r_A_m}} m, r(L) = {{taper_r_L_m}} m, and J(0) = {{taper_J_A_m4}} m4.

title: Differential Twist Relation
learningObjectives: Derive the local twist relation for the tapered shaft.
student: Write the differential relation for shaft rotation in terms of T, G, and r(x).

title: Angle-of-Twist Integral
student: Formulate the definite integral for rotation of end A relative to the fixed end.
instructor: φA = ∫0L 2T/[πG r(x)4] dx. The evaluated geometric integral ∫0L dx/r(x)4 is {{taper_integral_m_neg3}} m-3.

title: Numerical Angle of Twist
student: Evaluate the twist integral numerically and report the angle in radians and degrees.
gradingNotes: Numerical quadrature, a documented calculator integral, or equivalent computational evaluation is acceptable.

title: Maximum Torsional Shear Stress
learningObjectives: Calculate and locate the maximum stress in a tapered shaft.
student: Determine the maximum torsional shear stress and identify its location.
instructor: τmax(x) = 2T/[πr(x)3]. Because the radius is smallest at x = 0, the maximum occurs at the outer surface of end A: {{taper_tau_max_MPa}} MPa.

title: Compliance Localization and Sensitivity
learningObjectives: Explain why the small-end region controls twist and stress.
student: Explain why a modest increase in minimum radius can strongly reduce both stress and twist. Quantify how much of the assigned total twist accumulates in the first quarter of the shaft.
instructor: Stress varies as 1/r3 and the twist integrand as 1/r4, so the minimum-radius region has disproportionate influence. For the assigned profile, approximately {{taper_first_quarter_pct}}% of the total twist accumulates over 0 ≤ x ≤ L/4.

title: Stiffness Assessment and Recommendation
learningObjectives: Assess torsional stiffness and recommend a modification.
student: Compare the calculated rotation with the assigned allowable twist and make a limited mechanics-based recommendation.
instructor:
The twist utilization is {{taper_twist_utilization}}. {{taper_twist_assessment}}

{{taper_recommendation}}

Detailed design must also consider strength allowables, bending, attachment flexibility, stress concentrations, fatigue, dynamics, manufacturing limits, and applicable standards.
